title: Columbus Crew eliminate Messi and Inter Miami from MLS playoffs with stoppage-time strike
summary: Santiago Rodríguez strikes in stoppage time to seal win Inter Miami fail to defend 2025 MLS Cup title. Messi retired internationally earlier this year Inter Miami’s quest to defend their MLS Cup title is over. The South Florida side had two gilt-edged chances to take the lead in Game 2 of their best-of-three first-round series against Columbus in the MLS Playoffs on Friday, but missed both of them along with several others, later succumbing to a terrific stoppage-time winner from Santi Rodríguez in a 1-0 win for the Crew. title: USWNT seal Women’s World Cup qualification with 8-0 win over El Salvador
summary: US goes up 7-0 over El Salvador by half-time Win secures spot at 2027 World Cup and 2028 Olympics The United States’ place at a Women’s World Cup is treated as a foregone conclusion, but Friday’s all-or-nothing qualifier against El Salvador gave some reason for nerves. This was the first competitive game for Emma Hayes’ team since their Olympic gold medal match in August 2024, the end of two years of only friendlies. Given the global advances in women’s soccer over the years, maybe El Salvador could spring an all-time upset. The suspense ultimately lasted for eight minutes and 20 seconds. The USWNT opened the scoring in their Concacaf W Championship quarter-final with El Salvador in the ninth minute; a nifty training-ground set piece routine ending with Kennedy Wesley prodding the ball into the net, putting the hosts in the driver’s seat for an 8-0 win and a spot in next summer’s big show. With the win, the US maintains their perfect Women’s World Cup attendance record, a part of all 10 tournaments to date. Continue reading...

title: Aaron Rodgers texts into Amazon broadcast to defend himself as Steelers beat Broncos
summary: Denver Broncos 5-27 Pittsburgh Steelers Quarterback was released after blasting own coach At the end of a chaotic week that saw Aaron Rodgers’ highly public departure from Pittsburgh thanks to a rift with head coach Mike McCarthy – a turn of events that former coach Mike Tomlin called a “dumpster fire” and threatened to turn one of the league’s most stable franchises into a punchline – it felt on some level like The Steeler Way was at stake on Friday. Those Steelers left to navigate the fallout responded with a dominant 27-5 victory over the Denver Broncos that will turn down the volume, at least for a week. Continue reading...
